newsitem.title: UK: Nat'l Power leads utilities up on tax hopes.
newsitem.headline: Nat'l Power leads utilities up on tax hopes.

text.p: Shares in National Power PLc led UK utility shares higher on Monday after weekend reports that a windfall tax planned by the opposition Labour Party could be open to legal challenge, traders said.
By 1420 GMT, National Power was 12p higher at 490-1/2. PowerGen Plc was up 10p at 606 and United Utilities Plc gained 11-1/2p to 651-1/2.

"The sector has been doing very well recently and it's partly just up with the market today," one market-maker said. "But there seem to be more doubts creeping in about the windfall tax and that's been behind some buying today."

Labour, which is 20 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives in opinion polls with an election due by May 22, has said it will impose a windfall tax on Britain's privatised gas, electricity and water firms.
But the right-wing economic think-tank Aims of Industry said on Sunday that top lawyers it had consulted had suggested such a tax could be illegal under European Union law.
Labour insisted the plan was legal and would go ahead.
"Even if it is legal, it could get snarled up in legal action for years," another market-maker said. "It's certainly not a foregone conclusion"
Water shares were also strong with Anglian Water up 16p at 602-1/2, Thames Water up eight pence at 603-1/2 and Yorkshire Water 8-1/2p firmer at 722.
UK utilities shares have also benefited recently from safe-haven buying as they are not exposed to the impact of a stronger sterling, traders said.
